name: Literature gap

subjectOf.text: Dynamic regulation as part of institutional design in the evolution of law has not been systematically analyzed, despite an existing economics literature applying dynamic regulation to telecommunications, learning by doing, and principal-agent problems.
subjectOf.abstract: Dynamic regulation as part of institutional design in the evolution of law has not been systematically analyzed.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Evolution of Law Dynamic Regulation in a New Institutional Economics Framework (2013). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2267560

subjectOf.text: The existing literature on financial regulation has not adequately addressed the underlying causes and consequences of cyclical regulation.
subjectOf.abstract: The literature on financial regulation may not have addressed the underlying causes and consequences of cyclical regulation adequately.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Dynamic Regulation of the Financial Services Industry (2013). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2273857

subjectOf.text: Initiatives for sustainable financial regulation are largely missing, because anticipation of unknown future contingencies and preemption of possible future crises play no significant role either in the current regulatory framework or in the literature on financial regulation.
subjectOf.abstract: However, initiatives for sustainable financial regulation are still largely missing. Anticipation of unknown future contingencies and the preemption of possible future crises do not play a significant role in the current regulatory framework or in the literature on financial regulation.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Dynamic Regulation of the Financial Services Industry (2013). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2273857

subjectOf.text: Although some regulators use the term dynamic regulation in the context of SEC exemptive powers, the literature on financial regulation mostly ignores dynamic elements for regulation.
subjectOf.abstract: While some regulators use the term "dynamic regulation" in the context of SEC exemptive powers,112 the literature on financial regulation mostly ignores dynamic elements for regulation.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Dynamic Regulation of the Financial Services Industry (2013). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2273857

subjectOf.text: The decades long academic debate over improving fiduciary duty doctrine has overlooked Corporate Integrity Agreements entirely, even though the debate is otherwise framed as a choice between expanding and curtailing the doctrine.
subjectOf.abstract: The academic debate on options for improvement of the fiduciary duty doctrine has ignored the possible role of Corporate Integrity Agreements (CIAs).
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Elizabeth R. Malay, The Role of Corporate Integrity Agreements in the Expansion of Fiduciary Duties (2013). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2317580

subjectOf.text: No prior study had analyzed the performance implications of hedge fund adviser regulation, making this the first estimate of the causal effect of the Dodd-Frank Act registration requirement on hedge fund returns.
subjectOf.abstract: To our knowledge, no other study has analyzed the implications of hedge fund adviser regulation.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Barbara Luppi, Sandra Paterlini, Did the Dodd-Frank Act Impact Hedge Fund Performance (2014). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2389416

subjectOf.text: Because hedge funds developed under little or no regulatory supervision before the Dodd-Frank Act, the existing hedge fund performance literature largely fails to assess the implications of hedge fund regulation.
subjectOf.abstract: Because hedge funds evolved in a regulatory environment with low or no regulatory supervision until the enactment of the Dodd-Frank Act, most prior studies on hedge fund performance do not assess the implications of hedge fund regulation.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Barbara Luppi, Sandra Paterlini, Did the Dodd-Frank Act Impact Hedge Fund Performance (2014). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2389416
scope_conditions: pre Dodd-Frank Act hedge fund performance literature

subjectOf.text: Prior scholarship on the corporate governance effects of non and deferred prosecution agreements rests largely on anecdotal evidence and individual case studies rather than on systematic evidence, which is why its conclusions about those effects are unreliable.
subjectOf.abstract: The evaluation of issues pertaining to the effect of N/DPAs on corporate governance in prior studies is largely based on anecdotal evidence and valuable case studies.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Timothy Lacine, The Effect of Deferred and Non-Prosecution Agreements on Corporate Governance Evidence from 1993-20 (2014). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2486570

subjectOf.text: The existing literature has barely engaged the financial market implications of N/DPAs, which is the gap this study fills.
subjectOf.abstract: The literature has only marginally recognized the implications of N/DPAs for financial markets.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Timothy Lacine, Stock Price Response to Non- and Deferred Prosecution Agreements (2015). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2629451
scope_conditions: legal and governance literature on N/DPAs as of 2015

subjectOf.text: Because private funds evolved under low or no regulatory supervision until Dodd-Frank, the large prior literature on private fund performance largely does not assess the implications of private fund regulation, leaving a gap this study fills.
subjectOf.abstract: Because private funds evolved in a regulatory environment with low or no regulatory supervision until the enactment of the Dodd-Frank Act, most prior studies on private fund performance do not assess the implications of private fund regulation.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Barbara Luppi, Sandra Paterlini, Did the Dodd-Frank Act Impact Private Fund Performance  – Evidence from 2010 – 2015 (2016). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2816408
scope_conditions: private fund performance literature before Dodd-Frank

subjectOf.text: Beyond the authors' own prior work, there is no other empirical evidence on the effects of the Dodd-Frank Act on the private fund industry.
subjectOf.abstract: We are not aware of any other empirical evidence on the effects of the Dodd-Frank Act on the private fund industry.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Barbara Luppi, Sandra Paterlini, Did the Dodd-Frank Act Impact Private Fund Performance  – Evidence from 2010 – 2015 (2016). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2816408
scope_conditions: as of the paper's writing in 2016
